construction: Constructed by opus-rules-researcher (M02) on 2026-09-23 directly from the captured source text (docs/rules/sources/ecfr-14cfr260.txt, ecfr-14cfr254.txt, federal-web-pages-excerpts.md) and the spec. Not generated by, run through, or checked against any evaluator code.

conventions.fact_encoding: facts.<name> = {type, value, state}; state in {user_confirmed, extracted_candidate, derived, missing, conflicting}. money = {amount_minor:int, currency}. datetime = ISO-8601 with offset.
conventions.paths: R04.a = bag-fee refund (14 CFR 260.5); R04.b = delayed-bag incidental expenses (14 CFR 254.4 + DOT guidance); R04.c = lost/damaged property (14 CFR 254.4). Each case names the path(s) it tests.
conventions.delay_measurement: From deplane opportunity to delivery/pickup (260.5(a)). 'Within 12 hours' is inclusive of exactly 12:00 (spec assumption A1).
conventions.liability_floor: USD 4,700 per passenger for incidents on/after 2025-01-22; USD 3,800 before (FR-2024-23588). It is the lowest cap a carrier may impose, never an expected payout.
conventions.carrier_contract_terms: No carrier contract of carriage is captured in v1, so paths b/c are capped at likely_eligible_missing_evidence and their claim deadlines are unknown.
conventions.loader: A case has EITHER a top-level `expected` OR an `expected` on every variant. `clock` (and optional `source`) may be set on the case or on a variant; a variant value overrides the case value. `facts_from: <case id>` + `facts_override: {...}` means: copy that case's facts, then replace the named facts. A variant's `change` object replaces the named facts for that variant only. Every `facts` value is an object; no prose placeholders.
conventions.fact_states: user_confirmed | observed | derived | extracted_candidate | conflicting | missing | assumption. Contract §2.5 mapping: user_confirmed→confirmed, observed→observed, derived→derived, extracted_candidate→candidate, conflicting→conflicting, missing→missing (value null), assumption→assumption-class candidate. D147(2)/X1: `eligible` requires every decisive fact to be user_confirmed, or observed/derived from confirmed facts; an extracted_candidate decisive fact caps the outcome at likely_eligible_missing_evidence (the case lists it in expected.unconfirmed_decisive_facts). Since M2D the baseline cases use user_confirmed for decisive facts (the state after the user's fact review); each file has explicit cap variants.
conventions.conflicting: D152/D154 (README cross-pack rule 3): conflict_kind 'candidates' → different outcomes or amounts = needs_facts; same outcome and amount = capped at likely_eligible_missing_evidence (fact listed in unconfirmed_decisive_facts). conflict_kind 'confirmed_vs_observed' / 'confirmed_vs_confirmed' → manual_review. A conflicting or extracted-only deadline anchor never gives a firm date: deadline.date = null, status disputed_anchor / unknown_anchor, and (user-obligor paths only) advisory_act_by from the earliest candidate.
conventions.not_yet_due: D147(6)/X3: a path that is not ripe yet has outcome not_yet_due with expected.reevaluate_at (ISO date) or expected.reevaluate_when (event); never not_eligible.
conventions.missing_source: X5: a variant with source.record = 'missing' means no current source record exists for the pack → source_unverified.
conventions.path_a_eligible: D147(1): path a (bag-fee refund, 260.5) may reach eligible when its decisive facts are confirmed; the likely_eligible cap applies to paths b and c only (no carrier contract of carriage captured).

cases.title: Domestic bag delivered 13h15m after deplaning; MBR filed; fee paid to the carrier

service_type.note: D271 (extends D253(3)/D262 to path a): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved; an unknown service type caps the result at likely eligible (R04-17)

amount.formula: refund >= fee paid for that bag (260.5(e))

deadline.semantics: 260.5 requires a prompt refund; the regulation's 7-business/20-calendar-day definition is anchored to §260.6(a)(2) fare-refund events, so Recoup computes no date for bag fees.

justification.reasoning: Domestic bag not delivered within 12 hours of the deplane opportunity; MBR filed; the refund is automatic and at least the fee paid.
Extracted but unconfirmed decisive facts cap path a at likely_eligible.

expected.note: A lost bag needs no delay calculation (260.5 covers 'a lost bag or a significantly delayed checked bag').

justification.reasoning: Declared lost + MBR + fee paid → the bag-fee refund is due.

expected.reason: refund conditions met on 2024-09-13, before the part 260 bag-fee compliance date 2024-10-28 (spec §15 step 1b)

justification.reasoning: Path a does not evaluate events before the compliance date.

expected.note: Delivered 'within 12 hours' (inclusive; spec A1 — reviewer must confirm)

justification.reasoning: A significantly delayed bag is one 'not delivered ... within 12 hours'. Measured from the deplane opportunity.

cases.title: Bag 20 hours late; whether an MBR was filed is unknown

expected.question: Did you file a missing-bag report (Mishandled Baggage Report) with the airline? If so, add its reference number.
expected.note: If the answer is 'no', the outcome is not_yet_due with reevaluate_when 'MBR filed' (variant R04-03b).

justification.reasoning: The carrier has no refund obligation 'unless a passenger files a Mishandled Baggage Report'. Missing is not false.

expected.next_action: file a Mishandled Baggage Report with the operating carrier

justification.reasoning: The refund duty arises only after an MBR; the path is not ripe, not ineligible.

forbidden_outputs: a per-day cap applied by Recoup

justification.reasoning: Reimbursement is for 'reasonable, verifiable, and actual' expenses. Only documented lines are estimated (mission §10: use actual supported expenses). The $4,700 figure is a floor on the carrier's cap, not a payout.

cases.mission_domain_fixture: baggage-fee path separate from property/expense claims

bag_fee_merchant_of_record.note: fee charged by an online travel agency

totals.note: the bag fee and the expenses are different loss lines; the 3,500 fee must not also appear as an expense line; neither amount is confirmed recovery

justification.reasoning: Part 260 refunds the fee; part 254 liability covers delay damages. Mission §10 requires the two to stay separate. DOT-REF-8: request bag-fee refunds from the airline even when an agent was the merchant of record.

bag_status.evidence: carrier email 2026-09-20 'your bag has been declared lost'

carrier_exclusions.note: many contracts exclude electronics on domestic travel (DOT-BAG-7)

amount.reason: depreciation, contract exclusions, and the carrier's limit are unknown
amount.cap_display: Carrier liability limit: at least $4,700 per passenger (federal floor on the carrier's cap)

justification.reasoning: The limit version is selected by the incident date.

cases.title: Bag delayed because the passenger did not recheck it at the first US entry point

service_type.note: D271 (extends D253(3)/D262 to path a): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved

exemption_facts.evidence: carrier MBR note: bag left at JFK customs hall

expected.note: The 20h delay exceeds the 15h international standard, but the delay resulted from the CBP recheck failure. Path b/c for this international itinerary is unsupported (treaty), not 'not eligible'.

justification.reasoning: 260.5(f)(1) exempts delays resulting from 'failure to pick up and recheck a bag at the first international entry point'.

expected.note: 260.5(f)(2) exempts only 'if documented by the carrier'; with no carrier documentation the exemption does not apply and the 20 h domestic delay qualifies.

justification.reasoning: The (f)(2) exemption requires carrier documentation.

cases.title: International itinerary: expense path unsupported; bag-fee path still applies (15h standard)

service_type.note: D271 (extends D253(3)/D262 to path a): recorded so this case's expected outcome is preserved

results.note: International carriage: Montreal Convention (1,519 SDR per DOT-BAG-4), not 14 CFR 254. Not evaluated in v1.
segment > 12 h → 30 h standard; 30h01m exceeds it

justification.reasoning: Part 254 applies to interstate/intrastate transportation. Part 260's bag-fee rule covers international covered flights with the 15h/30h standards.

expected.question: The courier record says 9:10 am and you said 10:30 am. Do you have the delivery notice or a photo timestamp?
forbidden_outputs: choosing the user's time without evidence

justification.reasoning: The end of the delay is the delivery time; the two candidates fall on opposite sides of 12 hours.

expected.note: Both candidates exceed 12 h: the conflict is not material, but the fact is unconfirmed.

cases.title: User-confirmed delivery time contradicts the courier's delivery scan (confirmed vs observed)

expected.explanation: You said the bag arrived at 10:55; the courier's scan says 08:30. The 12-hour threshold depends on which is right. Check the courier notification or door-camera time.

justification.reasoning: Confirmed vs observed → manual review.

cases.title: Path b: a carousel pickup 20 minutes after deplaning is not on its own a delayed bag (M27 erratum E-R04-1, D234(9))

expected.note: Every pickup ends after the deplane opportunity, so a 20-minute span is not on its own a delay (spec §15 step 3.2). A confirmed Mishandled Baggage Report would meet the delay condition; a confirmed 'no report' gives not_eligible (R04-14b).
forbidden_outputs: an estimate of 2,500 from a 20-minute carousel pickup
treating any pickup after the deplane opportunity as a delayed bag

justification.reasoning: Part 254 speaks of 'delay in delivery' and sets no threshold (spec L12); the lead's ruling requires a confirmed mishandled-baggage report or a confirmed late delivery, and a carousel pickup alone is not a delay.

expected.note: Confirmed no report and a 20-minute pickup: no delay on path b (D234(9); spec §15 step 3.4).

justification.reasoning: Neither a confirmed report nor a confirmed late delivery.

bag_status.evidence: damage report filed at the baggage office

bag_delivered_or_picked_up_at.note: picked up from the carousel, damaged

expected.note: The report records damage to a bag that arrived with the passenger (25 minutes). The damage is claimed on path c, not as a delay on path b (D234(9); spec §15 step 3.3).

justification.reasoning: An MBR is also filed for damaged or pilfered bags, so with a short span it does not show a delay.

amount.cap_display: Carrier liability limit: at least $4,700 per passenger (federal floor on the carrier's cap)

expected.note: A confirmed delivery 36 hours after the deplane opportunity is a confirmed late delivery (spec §15 step 3.1(ii), assumption A5), which meets the delay condition without a report. Path b stays capped (no carrier contract captured).

justification.reasoning: The lead's ruling accepts a confirmed late delivery in place of a report; only documented, unallocated lines are estimated.

amount.cap_display: Carrier liability limit: at least $4,700 per passenger (federal floor on the carrier's cap)

expected.note: Under the literal words of D234(9), a confirmed mishandled-baggage report meets the path-b delay condition (spec §15 step 3.1(i)); only a damaged or pilfered bag with a short span is carved out (step 3.3, R04-14c). Here the status is a confirmed 'delivered', so the 20-minute span does not defeat the condition. The lead has not yet confirmed this reading (errata review item, ERR-R1-03); if the lead rules otherwise, this variant and step 3.1 change together before the errata are committed. Path b stays capped (no carrier contract captured).

justification.reasoning: The lead's ruling accepts a confirmed report as meeting the delay condition; only documented, unallocated lines are estimated.

expected.note: With a confirmed report and a 20-minute pickup, the bag's status decides path b: 'delivered' meets the delay condition (R04-14e); 'damaged' or 'pilfered' gives not_eligible, because the report may record damage rather than a delay (spec §15 step 3.3, R04-14c). This is the spec §15 step 3.5 example, on the same reading of D234(9) as R04-14e.

justification.reasoning: Missing is not false: under step 3.3 the status can still meet or defeat the delay condition.

cases.title: Path a: declared-lost bag with a 260.5(f)(1) recheck exemption fact (M27 erratum E-R04-2, D234(12))

bag_status.evidence: carrier email 2026-09-21 'your bag has been declared lost'

expected.reason: The airline declared the bag lost. 260.5(f) exempts 'the fee for a significantly delayed bag' where 'the delay resulted from' the passenger's failure to recheck it. Part 260 names lost and significantly delayed bags separately, but its definition of a significantly delayed bag ('not delivered ... within 12 hours') also fits a lost bag. The captured text does not settle whether the exemption reaches a lost bag (spec L11).
forbidden_outputs: not_eligible from the (f)(1) exemption for a declared-lost bag
eligible that sets the (f)(1) exemption aside

justification.reasoning: Two readings of the captured text are open (spec L11); a person reviews the case rather than Recoup resolving the point either way.

exemption_documented_by_carrier.evidence: carrier letter: bag not collected at the ticketed destination

expected.reason: The (f)(2) pickup exemption is documented by the carrier, but the bag was declared lost; whether (f)(2) reaches a lost bag is not settled by the captured text (spec L11).

justification.reasoning: Same open question as R04-15, for (f)(2).

expected.note: Control, unchanged from the approved §6: the voluntary-separation exemption does not reach a lost bag, because 260.5(g) forbids requiring a waiver of 'the right to a refund of bag fees if the bag is lost'.

justification.reasoning: Declared lost + MBR + fee paid; (f)(3) does not apply to a lost bag.

expected.note: With the (f)(1) exemption confirmed and no delivery time, the bag's status decides the result: delivered → not_eligible; still undelivered → not_yet_due (R04-15f); declared lost → manual_review. The delivery time itself is not asked (spec §15 step 2.3).

justification.reasoning: Missing is not false; only bag_status can change the outcome here.

bag_status.evidence: carrier message 2026-09-22: the bag has not been located yet

expected.note: The passenger agreed to travel without the bag (260.5(f)(3)), and the bag is confirmed still undelivered with no delivery time. A delivery would make the exemption apply (not_eligible); a loss declaration would keep 'the right to a refund of bag fees if the bag is lost' (260.5(g)) and give the R04-15c refund. Neither has happened, so path a is not yet due (README cross-pack rule 4). The awaited event is not the user's own action, so the next action is a wait (spec §15 step 2.3).
forbidden_outputs: not_eligible while the bag is still undelivered
eligible from the still-undelivered status extrapolated to the evaluation clock

justification.reasoning: The outcome depends on whether the bag is delivered or declared lost; a path that is not ripe is not_yet_due, never not_eligible.

bag_status.evidence: carrier message 2026-09-22: the bag has not been located yet

expected.note: The passenger did not recheck the bag at the first US entry point (260.5(f)(1)), and the bag is confirmed still undelivered with no delivery time. A delivery gives not_eligible (R04-07); a loss declaration gives manual_review (R04-15, spec L11). Until one happens, path a is not yet due (spec §15 step 2.3).
forbidden_outputs: not_eligible while the bag is still undelivered

justification.reasoning: Same as R04-15e, for the (f)(1) exemption.

bag_status.evidence: carrier email text 'your bag is still delayed' (not confirmed)

expected.note: An extracted 'still undelivered' status is not decisive (D234(1)): a not-yet-due verdict never rests on an unconfirmed candidate. The status decides between not_eligible (delivered), not_yet_due (still undelivered) and a refund (declared lost; R04-15c), so the user is asked to confirm it (spec §15 step 2.3).

justification.reasoning: The candidate is listed as candidate_unconfirmed and asked.

cases.title: Path a: bag confirmed still undelivered 14 hours after deplaning, with no delivery time (v1 does not extrapolate; V2-1, D234(10))

expected.note: The clock is 14 hours after the deplane opportunity, but a status value carries no as-of time, so v1 does not treat 'still undelivered' as a delivery time past the 12-hour threshold (spec §15 step 2.4; v2 item V2-1).
forbidden_outputs: eligible from a 'still missing' status extrapolated to the evaluation clock

justification.reasoning: §15 step 2.4: missing either instant and the bag not yet declared lost → needs_facts.

cases.title: Service type unknown on R04-01's otherwise-eligible facts: capped at likely eligible with the labelled assumption (D271, extends D253(3)/D262 to path a)

expected.note: R04-01's facts with the service type unknown. D270(3)/D271 extend R02's A8 (D253(3)/D262) to path a: an unknown service type never resolves toward eligible — capped at likely_eligible with the labelled assumption, asked because it is the only thing between likely and eligible (mirrors R02-15). D270(4): the next action stays track, never escalate — path a has no carrier timer at all (L6, 260.5 sets no day count for bag fees), so this is unaffected either way; see the pack's own m27c regression test for the explicit nextAction assertion.

justification.reasoning: 14 CFR 260.5's bag-fee refund duty runs with 260.2's covered-flight definition ('a scheduled flight'). With the service type unknown that condition is unknown. D270(3)/D271: no exception to README rule 5 for path a either — capped at likely_eligible with the assumption 'assumes a regularly scheduled flight', mirroring R02-15.

cases.title: Known public charter on R04-01's facts: unsupported before the MBR/exemption/delay questions (D271, extends D253(3) to path a)

service_type.evidence: booking confirmation: public charter operator disclosure

expected.note: A known non-scheduled service decides applicability before the MBR, exemption and delay questions, same as R02-16. 'Unsupported' is not 'not eligible': R04 v1 does not evaluate a charter's bag fee.

justification.reasoning: 14 CFR 260.5's duty runs with 260.2's covered-flight definition ('a scheduled flight'); 254.2 names 'charter or scheduled passenger service' separately. D270(3)/D271: a known non-scheduled value → unsupported, mirroring R02-16.
